name: Achish
bio:
Achish was the king of Gath. Fleeing from Saul, David at one point took refuge in Gath, but Achish's officials recognized him as the very David the women sang about — "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands" — leaving David afraid. He pretended to be insane in front of Achish, scratching on the doors of the gate and letting saliva run down his beard. Achish said to his servants, "Look at the man! He is insane! Why bring him to me? Am I so short of madmen that you have to bring this fellow here to carry on like this in front of me? Must this man come into my house?" and had David driven away (1 Samuel 21:10-15). David escaped this danger and continued his years as a fugitive.

David later fled to Achish again at Gath, this time with six hundred men and their households; Achish gave him the town of Ziklag to settle in, and David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months (1 Samuel 27:1-7). During this time David raided the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites while falsely reporting to Achish that he had attacked the Negev of Judah; Achish, believing him, became convinced David had made himself utterly odious to his own people and would be his servant forever (1 Samuel 27:8-12). This relationship of surface trust and mutual scheming between Achish and David would continue to develop in the chapters ahead, especially on the eve of the battle at Gilboa.
